help.title: Help
help.swagger_description: Swagger UI - Interactive REST API explorer
help.open_tor: Open Tor Browser and wait for it to connect
help.paste_onion: Copy the onion address above and paste it into Tor Browser's address bar
help.rest_intro: The REST API is the primary interface: every feature of the web UI is available through it. All endpoints live under {endpoint}, answer application/json by default and wrap results as {ok_example} (errors: {error_example}). Add .txt or send Accept: text/plain for plain text.
help.graphql_endpoint: The GraphQL endpoint is {graphql}; the OpenAPI spec is served at {swagger}.
help.web_create_title: Create a paste via the web
help.web_create_body: Go to /create, fill in your content, choose a language and expiry, then click Create Paste. Save the delete token — it is shown only once.
help.burn_body: Set burn_after to a number 1–9999. The paste is deleted after that many views. Set to 0 to disable.
help.compat_intro: Compatibility endpoints are separate from the native API above. They reproduce the wire protocol of other paste services so existing scripts and CLIs work unmodified. Compat creates are anonymous (any API key is accepted and ignored) and use each service's own delete convention, not the owner token.
help.compat_dropin: This server is a drop-in replacement for multiple paste services. Point existing scripts and CLIs here without modification:
help.wire_compat: Wire-compatible with the {name} API:
help.sk_row_create: Create paste (form text/title/name/lang/expire/private; apikey accepted and ignored); returns the view URL {view_url} as plain text, or Error: <msg>
help.sk_row_view: Redirects to the native paste view
help.hb_row_create: Create paste from the raw request body; returns {key_example}
help.hb_row_get: Get paste content as {data_example} ({missing_example} if missing)
help.dp_row_create: Create paste; format=url returns bare URL, format=json returns JSON
help.curlupload_intro: Wire-compatible with the curl-upload one-liner family:
help.curlupload_row: Upload via multipart file (0x0.st), form sprunge (sprunge.us), or form f:1 (ix.io); returns a bare raw-content URL {raw_url}. Requests with none of these fields fall through to the native paste-create handler.
help.curlupload_token: The 0x0.st style also returns an X-Token response header — the paste's compat delete token, mirroring the 0x0.st management-token convention.
help.termbin_intro: Wire-compatible with termbin.com and the fiche server protocol. Connect, stream content, close the write side; the server replies with the paste URL and closes:
help.termbin_limits: Maximum payload: {size} bytes. Idle/read timeout: {timeout}. TCP port: {port}.
help.subdomain_intro: Any target can also be reached by using its label as the leftmost part of the hostname (for example hb. before this server's hostname). On a matched subdomain, a bare POST / with a raw body creates a paste for that target, and other targets' routes are hidden.
help.tor_intro: This service is available as a Tor hidden service for enhanced privacy.
help.tor_step_paste: Paste the onion address above into the Tor Browser address bar
help.tor_privacy_note: Using Tor hides your IP address and encrypts your connection through the Tor network.
help.i2p_intro: This service is available as an I2P eepsite for enhanced privacy.
help.i2p_step_install: Install I2P or i2pd and wait for it to integrate with the network
help.i2p_step_proxy: Configure your browser to use the I2P HTTP proxy (default 127.0.0.1:4444)
help.i2p_step_paste: Copy the .b32.i2p address above and paste it into your browser address bar
help.i2p_note: Using I2P routes your connection through the I2P network. Eepsites are served over http:// — the I2P tunnel provides the transport encryption, so no TLS certificate is used.
help.faq_q_account: Do I need an account or API key?
help.faq_a_account: No. Creating, reading, and deleting pastes requires no authentication. The delete token returned at creation is all you need to remove a paste.
help.faq_a_retention: Until their expiry elapses (see the expiry table above) or their burn-after view count is reached. Pastes set to never are kept until deleted.
help.faq_a_size: Yes. The server enforces a maximum paste size of {size}; oversized content is rejected with a 413 response.
help.faq_q_scripts: Can I use it from scripts?
help.faq_a_scripts: Yes — pipe to curl --data-binary @-, use the JSON API, or point existing pastebin.com scripts at this server.
help.ts_404_body: The paste ID is wrong or the paste has expired or been burned. Check the URL.
help.ts_413_body: Your content exceeds the maximum paste size. Split it or reduce the size.
help.ts_429_body: You have hit the rate limit. Wait and retry; the Retry-After header tells you how long.
help.ts_403_body: The delete token is missing or incorrect. Only the correct token can delete a paste.
help.mcp_meta_description: Connect an AI assistant to {site} through MCP
help.mcp_overview_body: {site} provides a remote MCP server over Streamable HTTP. Every public API operation is available to an assistant as a tool.
help.mcp_auth_body: Send credentials in Authorization: Bearer {token}. This uses the same tokens as the REST API. Public tools also work anonymously. For owner access, create a linked token for this client at /server/preferences/tokens, then revoke it separately when no longer needed. Do not use the primary owner token or the operator token.
help.mcp_no_tools: No public tools are currently registered.
help.mcp_auth_tools_note: Authenticated callers may see additional tools when their token has the required access.
help.mcp_behavior_body: The endpoint accepts POST requests only and keeps no sessions. Calls use the same rate limits and audit handling as the API. Present Origin headers are validated. Supported protocol versions:
help.mcp_error_400: Check the MCP protocol version and required request headers.
help.mcp_error_401: The token is missing, invalid, or expired. Send a valid Bearer token; the response includes WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.
help.mcp_error_403: The Origin was rejected or the token lacks access. Use the correct site origin and an appropriate linked token.
help.mcp_error_404: MCP is disabled for this server.
help.mcp_error_405: The endpoint is POST-only; use POST for MCP requests.

privacy.default_data_collection:
**Information handled to provide the service:**

- Paste content and the optional title, language, expiry, visibility, and burn-after-read settings you submit
- IP address and request details used for rate limiting, abuse prevention, and security logs
- Owner tokens, stored as a SHA-256 hash with an encrypted recoverable copy; compatibility protocols may use their own delete tokens
- Theme, language, and consent preferences stored in browser cookies
- If an operator enables analytics and a visitor consents, the configured provider receives the analytics data described in the Cookies section

GeoIP country information is derived from the IP address using a downloaded database; the visitor's IP is not sent to a GeoIP lookup service.
privacy.default_data_usage:
**Information is used to:**

- Create, display, retrieve, and delete pastes according to their settings and the applicable owner or compatibility delete token
- Apply expiry and burn-after-read deletion
- Operate the service, enforce rate limits, prevent abuse, and investigate security events
- Store visitor preferences and record consent choices
- Provide analytics only when an operator has configured a provider and the visitor has consented
- Deliver contact-form messages to the configured recipient when email delivery is enabled

Cairnbin has no user accounts, paid tiers, or targeted advertising.
privacy.default_data_usage_sold:
**Information is used to:**

- Create, display, retrieve, and delete pastes according to their settings and the applicable owner or compatibility delete token
- Apply expiry and burn-after-read deletion
- Operate the service, enforce rate limits, prevent abuse, and investigate security events
- Store visitor preferences and record consent choices
- Provide analytics only when an operator has configured a provider and the visitor has consented
- Deliver contact-form messages to the configured recipient when email delivery is enabled

The operator has configured this instance to sell or share data. The categories and conditions are listed in the data-sharing section below; use the opt-out control on this page to record a device-level opt-out.
privacy.default_data_security:
**How information is protected:**

- Owner and compatibility delete tokens are stored as hashes; owner tokens also have an encrypted recoverable copy
- Paste and token data are stored in the database configured by the operator (local SQLite by default, or remote libSQL/Turso when configured)
- Public-site connections use HTTPS/TLS; Tor and I2P addresses use their overlay network transport
- Operator actions are subject to access controls and audit logging
- Backups can be encrypted by the operator

swagger.if_true_content_is_a_redirect_target_url: If true, content is a redirect target URL, not paste text
swagger.paste_body_text_if_the_entire_trimmed_co: Paste body text. If the entire trimmed content is exactly one http:// or https:// URL and nothing else, the paste is auto-detected as a link (is_link=true in the response) — there is no request field to set this explicitly
swagger.chroma_language_identifier_omit_for_auto: Chroma language identifier; omit for auto-detect; ignored when content is auto-detected as a link
swagger.delete_after_n_views_0_disabled_max_9999: Delete after N views (0 = disabled; max 9999)
swagger.returns_a_paginated_list_of_recent_publi: Returns a paginated list of recent public pastes.
swagger.creates_a_new_paste_accepts_json_or_mult: Creates a new paste. Accepts JSON or multipart/form-data.
swagger.returns_paste_metadata_and_content_by_id: Returns paste metadata and content by ID. If the paste is a link (is_link=true), responds with a 302 redirect to the target URL instead of a JSON body — use the /raw endpoint to retrieve the target URL as text without redirecting.
swagger.paste_is_a_link_redirects_to_the_target_: Paste is a link; redirects to the target URL
swagger.deletes_a_paste_requires_authorization_b: Deletes a paste. Requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header (the delete token returned at creation time).
swagger.returns_the_raw_paste_text_as_plain_text: Returns the raw paste text as plain text. For links (is_link=true), returns the target URL as plain text without redirecting.
swagger.returns_server_health_status_and_basic_m: Returns server health status and basic metrics.
swagger.returns_the_server_version_commit_id_and: Returns the server version, commit ID, and build date.
swagger.returns_the_openapi_3_0_3_json_specifica: Returns the OpenAPI 3.0.3 JSON specification for this API.
swagger.executes_a_graphql_query_or_mutation_the: Executes a GraphQL query or mutation. The interactive GraphiQL explorer is available at /server/docs/graphql.
swagger.graphql_request_with_query_and_optional_: GraphQL request with query and optional variables.
swagger.wire_compatible_with_the_pastebin_com_ap: Wire-compatible with the pastebin.com API (https://pastebin.com/doc_api). Dispatches on `api_option`: `paste` (default) creates a paste; `list` returns recent public pastes as XML; `delete` removes a paste; `userdetails` returns a stub XML user record. `api_dev_key` and `api_user_key` are silently ignored.
swagger.paste_url_plain_text_or_xml_response_dep: Paste URL (plain text) or XML response depending on api_option
swagger.wire_compatible_with_pastebin_com_raw_co: Wire-compatible with pastebin.com raw content endpoint. Returns the paste body as plain text.
swagger.wire_compatible_stub_always_returns_anon: Wire-compatible stub. Always returns ANONYMOUS. Required by tools that call this endpoint before creating pastes.
swagger.wire_compatible_with_the_microbin_api_ht: Wire-compatible with the microbin API (https://github.com/szabodanika/microbin). Accepts form fields: `content`, `title`, `syntax`, `expiry`, `burn_after_reads`, `private`.
swagger.returns_a_list_of_pastes_in_microbin_jso: Returns a list of pastes in microbin JSON format.
swagger.returns_a_single_paste_by_id_in_microbin: Returns a single paste by ID in microbin JSON format.
swagger.wire_compatible_with_the_lenpaste_api_ht: Wire-compatible with the lenpaste API (https://github.com/forksmgr/lcomrade-lenpaste). Also available at `/api/v1/new`. Accepts form fields: `text`, `title`, `syntax`, `ttl` (seconds), `oneUse`.
swagger.returns_a_paste_by_id_in_lenpaste_json_f: Returns a paste by ID in lenpaste JSON format. Also available at `/api/v1/get`.
swagger.deletes_a_paste_also_available_at_api_v1: Deletes a paste. Also available at `/api/v1/remove` and via GET for legacy clients.
swagger.returns_a_paginated_list_of_pastes_in_le: Returns a paginated list of pastes in lenpaste JSON format. Also available at `/api/v1/list`.
swagger.returns_server_metadata_in_lenpaste_json: Returns server metadata in lenpaste JSON format: title, description, admin contact, limits, and syntax list.
swagger.wire_compatible_with_the_stikked_api_htt: Wire-compatible with the stikked API (https://github.com/claudehohl/Stikked). Returns the new paste URL as plain text.
swagger.returns_paste_metadata_and_content_in_st: Returns paste metadata and content in stikked JSON format.
swagger.wire_compatible_with_the_haste_server_ap: Wire-compatible with the haste-server API (https://github.com/toptal/haste-server). Accepts raw body or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` with `data` field. Returns `{"key":"<id>"}` as JSON.
swagger.returns_document_content_in_hastebin_jso: Returns document content in hastebin JSON format: `{"key":"…","data":"…"}`.
swagger.wire_compatible_with_the_dpaste_api_http: Wire-compatible with the dpaste API (https://github.com/bartTC/dpaste). Also available at `/api/v2/`. `format=url` returns a bare URL; `format=json` returns JSON with `url` and `content` fields. Accepts `lexer`, `expires` (seconds), and `title` fields.
swagger.paste_url_plain_text_or_json_depending_o: Paste URL (plain text) or JSON depending on format param
swagger.wire_compatible_with_the_curl_upload_one: Wire-compatible with the curl-upload one-liner family: 0x0.st (`-F file=@…`), sprunge (`-F sprunge=<-`), and ix.io (`-F f:1=<-`). Also accepts a raw request body. Returns the paste URL as plain text. When called with `Accept: application/json` or `?json`, returns `{"ok":true,"url":"…","delete_token":"…"}`.
swagger.upload_via_file_field_sprunge_field_f_1_: Upload via file field, sprunge field, f:1 field, or raw body
swagger.paste_url_as_plain_text_or_json_when_req: Paste URL as plain text (or JSON when requested)
swagger.info_description: A fast, anonymous cairnbin service with REST and GraphQL APIs. Compatible with pastebin.com, microbin, lenpaste, stikked, hastebin/haste-server, dpaste, 0x0.st, sprunge.us, ix.io, and termbin/fiche.

cli.maintenance_help:
Maintenance commands:

backup [file] - Create and verify an archive of service data
  Default: {backup_dir}/{project_name}_backup_YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS.tar.gz
  --include-ssl includes ssl/; --include-data includes the data directory
backup test - Verify the security keypair without creating a backup
restore <file> - Restore an archive; the server stops and restarts
update [cmd] - Manage updates: check, yes (install), or branch <stable|beta|devel>
mode <mode> - Set production or development mode
setup - Reset server configuration (first run or root only)
pgp <action> - Manage the security keypair
  generate | rotate | publish | export public [path] | export private <path> | import <file> | delete
token <action> - list | revoke <prefix>
data <action> <prefix> - export or delete paste data by owner-token prefix
secret rotate <name> - Rotate installation_secret or encryption_key
compliance report - Print the compliance status summary

Examples:
  {project_name} --maintenance backup
  {project_name} --maintenance restore backup.tar.gz
  {project_name} --maintenance mode development
  {project_name} --maintenance pgp generate
  {project_name} --maintenance token list
  {project_name} --maintenance data export tok_abc123
  {project_name} --maintenance compliance report
cli.update_help:
Update management:

check - Check for available updates; compare the installed version with the latest release
yes - Download and install the latest update, replace the binary, and restart
branch <name> - Choose the release channel: stable (default), beta, or devel

Examples:
  {binary} --update check
  {binary} --update yes
  {binary} --update branch beta

cli.shell_help_full:
Shell integration commands:

  completions [SHELL]   Print shell completion script
                        Auto-detects shell if SHELL omitted
                        Supported: bash, zsh, fish, sh, dash, ksh, powershell, pwsh

  init [SHELL]          Print shell init command for eval
                        Auto-detects shell if SHELL omitted

Usage:
  # Add to shell profile for persistent completions
  # bash
  {binary} --shell init >> ~/.bashrc
  # zsh
  {binary} --shell init >> ~/.zshrc
  # fish
  {binary} --shell init >> ~/.config/fish/config.fish

  # Or eval directly for current session
  eval "$({binary} --shell init)"

  # Generate completion script only
  {binary} --shell completions bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/{binary}

security.title: Security
security.meta_description: How to report a security vulnerability in {site} — contact channels, disclosure policy, and encryption key
security.how_to_report_text: If you believe you have found a security vulnerability, please report it privately through one of the channels below, in order of preference. Do not open a public issue or disclose the details until we have had a chance to investigate and coordinate a fix.
security.channel_form_text: Following this link opens the security-report form; the report body is encrypted at rest and never stored in plaintext.
security.encryption_text: For sensitive details, encrypt your report with our PGP public key, available at:
security.link_policy_desc: scope, safe harbor, and coordinated-disclosure window
security.link_txt_desc: the machine-readable version of this page (RFC 9116)
security.policy_meta_description: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy for {site} — scope, safe harbor, and how to report
security.reporting_text: We welcome reports from security researchers. Reports are submitted through a rotating, single-use link published in our security.txt file. Following that link opens an encrypted reporting form; the report body is encrypted at rest and is never stored in plaintext.
security.pgp_available: Our PGP public key for encrypting sensitive details is available at:
security.disclosure_window_text: We ask that you give us up to {days} days to investigate and remediate a reported issue before any public disclosure, or until a coordinated disclosure date is mutually agreed — whichever comes first. We will keep you updated through your report's status page.
security.in_scope_1: This service and its official domains
security.in_scope_3: The public REST, GraphQL, and web endpoints
security.out_scope_1: Denial-of-service, volumetric, or rate-limit exhaustion testing
security.out_scope_2: Social engineering, phishing, or physical attacks against staff
security.out_scope_3: Automated scanner output without a demonstrated, reproducible impact
security.out_scope_4: Reports affecting only unsupported or end-of-life versions
security.out_scope_5: Attacks requiring a compromised host, rooted device, or physical access
security.safe_harbor_text: We will not pursue or support legal action against researchers who act in good faith, respect this policy, avoid privacy violations and data destruction, and give us reasonable time to respond before disclosing. Testing must stay within the scope above, use your own test data, and stop at the first sign of access to another user's data. Activity conducted consistently with this policy is considered authorized.
security.acknowledgments_text: With your permission, we credit researchers who report valid issues on our acknowledgments page.
security.status_rate_limited: This status link may only be opened once per day. You are seeing the last loaded state; please check back tomorrow for a fresh view.
security.status_contact_text: To add information to this report, reply to the acknowledgment email and include your tracking ID.
security.thanks_subtitle: Thank you to the researchers who help keep {site} safe
security.thanks_meta_description: Researchers we thank for responsibly disclosing security issues in {site}
security.thanks_intro: We are grateful to the following researchers for responsibly disclosing security issues under our security policy.
security.thanks_empty: No disclosures have been published yet. If you have found a security issue, please review our security policy and report it responsibly.
